First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨\frac{1}{t},\,\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)⟩\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨\frac{1}{t},\,\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)⟩\,\text{d}t & =⟨\int \frac{1}{t}\,\text{d}t,\,\int \pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡|t|+{c}_{1},\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)+{c}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The initial condition $F(1)=⟨-1,\,2⟩$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1)=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡|1|+{c}_{1},\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨-1,\,2⟩ \\ ⟨{c}_{1},\,1+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨-1,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${c}_{1}=-1$ and ${c}_{2}=1.$ Consequently

$$
F(t)=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡|t|-1,\,1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)⟩.
$$
